key_insight: The paper suggests that agents can learn game-playing skills from synthetic experience instead of depending only on expensive human demonstrations. This opens a scalable path to training more capable computer-use and game agents in rich, dynamic environments.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of training game-playing agents when real demonstrations are limited and interactive environments are hard to scale. Existing pipelines often miss rare or dynamic states, making learning incomplete and inefficient.
method: Generate synthetic experience to expand training coverage beyond what human demonstrations provide.
Use this synthetic data to teach agents how to act in visually rich game environments with diverse mechanics.
Build a learning pipeline aimed at improving robustness in dynamic and hard-to-cover game states.
impact: This matters because it reduces reliance on costly, narrow demonstration datasets and makes agent training more scalable. For practitioners, it suggests a practical route to improving general-purpose digital agents in complex interactive settings.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing synthetic experience generation feeding into agent training
A before-vs-after comparison of limited human demonstrations versus broader synthetic coverage
An illustration of a game screen with labeled keyboard/mouse actions
A chart showing improved state coverage or training efficiency
paper_title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
paper_authors: Mingyu Ouyang, Yiran Wang, Siyuan Hu, Xingyilang Yin, Huiqiang Sun
